profile.name: Hearth Home Appliances
profile.summary: US maker of kitchen and laundry appliances (~2,000 employees, factories in Tennessee and Ohio). Sells refrigerators, dishwashers, washing machines and microwaves through big-box stores and its own website. Imports some parts from Mexico and Asia. No food, no medicine, no vehicles.
businessLines: Retail and online sales with product warranties
applies: DOE energy and water efficiency standards for home appliances
Consumer product safety rules and recalls (CPSC)
EPA rules on refrigerants and chemicals in products
Tariffs and trade rules on imported appliance parts
Factory workplace safety (OSHA) and labor rules
doesNotApply: Food, drugs, medical devices, aviation, banking
Energy rules for power plants, pipelines or utilities

product-standards.description: Energy efficiency, product safety, recalls, refrigerants

items.title: Heightened Requirements for Foreign Importers of Record

deadline.verifyNote: matches FR API field on re-fetch

deadlines.quote: As explained in Section VII, licensed customs brokers may submit requests for delayed compliance with the changes in Sec.  111.29 of title 19 of the Code of Federal Regulations (19 CFR 111.29) prior to January 5, 2027.
deadlines.verifyNote: quote found verbatim in primary source

deadlines.quote: All customs brokers are expected to be in full compliance with the requirements of this rule no later than May 6, 2027.
deadlines.verifyNote: quote found verbatim in primary source

deadlines.quote: Comment date: Comments on the rule must be received on or before January 5, 2027.
deadlines.verifyNote: quote found verbatim in primary source

items.reason: CBP interim final rule imposes new requirements on foreign importers of record and customs brokers; Hearth's imports of parts from Mexico and Asia, whether through foreign IOR suppliers or its brokers, may face new entry requirements and compliance changes.
items.action: Direct Trade Compliance to identify suppliers and customs brokers affected by stricter foreign importer rules and confirm Mexico and Asia part shipments will keep clearing customs without delay.

items.title: Adjusting Imports of Robotics, Industrial Machinery, and Their Parts and Components Into the United States
items.reason: Presidential import adjustment (likely tariffs) on robotics, industrial machinery and their parts raises the cost of factory automation equipment for Hearth's Tennessee and Ohio plants.
items.action: Have Trade Compliance estimate how new import taxes on robotics and industrial machinery would raise automation equipment costs at the Tennessee and Ohio plants, and adjust capital purchase plans accordingly.

events.markdown:
# Regulatory triage — Hearth Home Appliances
Window 2026-11-02 → 2026-11-06 · as of 2026-11-06 · 2 items

## Critical (1)

- **Heightened Requirements for Foreign Importers of Record** [Federal Register]
  - Direct Trade Compliance to identify suppliers and customs brokers affected by stricter foreign importer rules and confirm Mexico and Asia part shipments will keep clearing customs without delay.
  - Deadline: 2027-01-05 (effective, FR field ✓) · Owner: Ken Adeyemi (Trade Compliance) · Areas: trade
  - 91 FR 69977 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/06/2026-22735/heightened-requirements-for-foreign-importers-of-record

## Low (1)

- **Adjusting Imports of Robotics, Industrial Machinery, and Their Parts and Components Into the United States** [Federal Register]
  - Have Trade Compliance estimate how new import taxes on robotics and industrial machinery would raise automation equipment costs at the Tennessee and Ohio plants, and adjust capital purchase plans accordingly.
  - Deadline: none found · Owner: Ken Adeyemi (Trade Compliance) · Areas: trade
  - 91 FR 69199 ✓ · https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/02/2026-22385/adjusting-imports-of-robotics-industrial-machinery-and-their-parts-and-components-into-the-united
